li.label: midsummer bonfire
li.description: Flames higher than the roof, everyone singing badly. The shortest night of the year, and the best.

li.label: beautiful flames
li.description: Did you see how high it went? Did you see the colors?

li.label: no celebration
li.description: Other people mark the seasons. We just work through them.

li.label: harvest home
li.description: The fields are in and we ate like kings to celebrate. Winter can do its worst.

li.label: a warm midwinter
li.description: The longest night, a full belly and everyone close to the fire.

li.label: midwinter stories
li.description: We sat up late telling stories about home. Some of them were even true.

li.label: a year named after me
li.description: They named the whole year after me. My name, in the annals. Forever, or until the paper burns.

li.label: someone's vanity indulged
li.description: A whole year named after one person. Who do they think they are?

li.label: a year for those we lost
li.description: This year carries the names of our dead. That feels right.

li.label: the year of the muffalo
li.description: We named the year after a muffalo. I laughed for an hour. The muffalo did not care.

li.label: first pick of the spoils
li.description: I fought hardest, and I got first pick. As it should be.

li.label: someone grabbed the best spoils
li.description: We all fought. One of us got the good boots.

li.label: fair shares
li.description: The spoils were split evenly. Nobody can complain. Some will anyway.

li.label: graves even for raiders
li.description: They came to kill us, and we buried them anyway. That's the difference between us.

li.label: bodies left for the animals
li.description: We left them out there for the scavengers. I can hear it at night.

li.label: victory feast
li.description: We beat them, and we ate like it. Alive and full. What a day.

li.label: they made me let my animal go
li.description: The council had my animal turned loose in the wild. I keep looking at the treeline.

li.label: hair in the stew
li.description: There's animal hair in everything I eat now. The council decided that was fine.

li.label: a tradition kept
li.description: We did it the way we always do. Some things out here stay the same, and that's a comfort.

li.label: a tradition broken
li.description: We've always done it. This year we didn't. It feels like something slipped.
